location.region: Uji and other regions (roasted from diverse harvests)

characteristics.cultivar: Various (often utilizing later-harvest bancha or tea stalks)
characteristics.oxidation: 0% (roasting is thermal processing, not enzyme oxidation)
characteristics.roast: Heavy — the defining process of this tea
characteristics.harvestSeason: Usually crafted from summer or autumn harvests (bancha)
characteristics.waterTemperature: 90–95°C (high heat extracts rich aromas without bitterness)

description.short: Roasted Japanese green tea with warm hazelnut and caramel aromas, boasting minimal caffeine
description.overview: The only style of Japanese green tea where, following steam fixation, leaves are subjected to high-heat drum roasting — transforming the green profile into toasty, coffee-like comfort.
description.leaf: Rich reddish-brown leaves and stems, visually unique among Japanese teas
description.liquor: Clear reddish-brown liquor, resembling amber tea rather than typical green tea
description.aroma: Toasted hazelnut, caramelized sugar, roasted grains, cocoa nuances
description.taste: Smooth, nutty, gently sweet, virtually free of astringency or bitterness
description.processing: Standard Japanese steaming → drying → high-temperature charcoal or drum roasting until leaf turns reddish-brown

history.origin: Created in Kyoto in the 1920s as a thrifty way to revitalize coarser bancha leaves and twigs by high-heat roasting.
history.development: Roasting drastically alters the leaf chemistry, pyrolyzing tannins and sublimating caffeine, making hojicha exceptionally easy on digestion.
history.modern: Today hojicha is a beloved daily drink in Japan, ideal for evening relaxation, and has become a global favorite in ice cream and roasted tea lattes.
interestingFacts: Due to its minimal caffeine levels, hojicha is traditionally given to children, seniors, and enjoyed as a soothing evening tea throughout Japan.
Roasting transforms inexpensive bancha and stems into an artisanal beverage celebrated for its rich, complex caramel notes.
